name: copy_sixteen_words_to_buffer
description: Copies sixteen consecutive 32-bit words from a fixed offset in the base register into a caller-supplied buffer, if the buffer pointer is non-null. It then calls through a function pointer held in another register.

name: install_program_handler_record
description: Finds the largest value stored in a linked list of entries and writes it into a new record, then fills that record with incrementing words. It copies a sixteen-word state block into the record, stores the copy routine as its handler, and copies the block back after a library call.

name: copy_sixteen_words_to_buffer
description: Copies sixteen consecutive 32-bit words from a fixed offset in the base register into a caller-supplied buffer, if the buffer pointer is non-null. It then calls through a function pointer held in another register.

name: parse_command_line_and_run
description: Splits the command line string into a table of argument pointers, handling quoted arguments and star escapes for newline and escape characters. It then runs the main routine and releases the message port, task and libraries it obtained.

name: release_startup_resources
description: Stores the parameter into a slot of the state structure reached through a global library pointer. It then closes the file, the library and the message port held in that structure when each is present, calling the matching library function for each.

name: start_workbench_tool
description: Opens the required system libraries and loads a tool entry, decoding global strings by XOR with a fixed byte before use. It reports a startup error when the tool or its resident tag cannot be found, and it reads the second argument variant to choose the start path.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns minus one when the first string is smaller at the first differing byte, one when it is larger, and zero when the strings are identical.

name: build_resource_list_from_table
description: Walks a chain of table entries, allocating an eight-byte node for each and storing in it the result of a lookup on the entry's value. The nodes are linked in order and the head is returned, or the partial list is returned if an allocation or lookup fails.

name: match_name_and_pad_field
description: Compares a global zero-terminated name against the text at the buffer pointer. When the buffer's byte at offset twenty is a two, it first writes a period and four spaces at offset seventeen before returning.

name: write_dot_and_padding
description: Writes a period followed by four spaces into five consecutive bytes of the buffer starting at offset seventeen. This pads a name field to a fixed width.

name: check_name_prefix_match
description: Walks the global zero-terminated name and the buffer pointer together, advancing both, until the name ends or the bytes differ. It returns no value.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so calling it performs no work and passes control straight back to the caller.

name: forward_call_with_stack_slot
description: Forwards its two parameters to another routine together with the address of a stack slot in the current frame, then returns.

name: format_buffer_and_forward_text
description: Calls a routine through a global pointer to fill a 140-byte stack buffer, then measures the zero-terminated text in it. When the text is not empty, it passes the text and its length to another routine.

name: scan_disk_block_bitmap
description: Writes a one- or two-digit count into a text field, clears a table of block entries, then walks a bit map of disk blocks, comparing flags of consecutive blocks and invoking routines for each change. The decompiled listing is cut off partway, so the later behaviour cannot be recovered.

name: clear_state_block_and_dispatch
description: Calls a routine, zeroes a block of roughly seven thousand words addressed through the base register, and stores a process pointer and a global pointer. It then calls one of two routines depending on the value returned by a library call.

name: allocate_buffers_and_init_state
description: Allocates several memory blocks of fixed sizes and stores the returned handles in globals, after referencing the text demo.pic. It then runs a fixed sequence of setup calls, repeating part of them when the parameter is below two.

name: start_copper_list_from_record
description: Reads a field from a record reached through a global base pointer and passes it to the routine that starts a copper list, which points the display co-processor at that list.

name: run_fixed_setup_calls
description: Makes four setup calls with fixed arguments taken from globals and constants, touches the interrupt enable register, and writes a constant to a global variable.

name: allocate_block_and_fill_slots
description: Allocates a block of about eleven hundred bytes and stores its address in a global. It fills eight consecutive slots with addresses spaced one hundred forty-four bytes apart, calls another routine, then copies two global values to new positions.

name: store_constant_and_call
description: Stores a fixed decimal constant into a field of a global-relative record and then calls another routine with no arguments.

name: call_with_global_pointer
description: Loads a pointer from a global table and calls another routine with that pointer and the fixed size of 1152, the size of the block allocated earlier.

name: call_two_global_pointers
description: Passes two pointers read from global variables, one after the other, to another routine.

name: forward_argument_to_library_call
description: Passes a global value and the low word of its argument to another routine, which invokes a library function through a vector.

name: forward_call_without_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns without any further action.

name: lookup_pair_and_dispatch
description: Searches a two-entry table in globals for the value passed as a parameter. When it is found, calls another routine with the matching partner value and stores the index reached in a global.

name: swap_globals_and_call
description: Exchanges the values of two global variables and then calls another routine with the swapped values as arguments.

name: open_graphics_and_intuition
description: Stores the base returned by an initial call and marks a field in it, then requests two further library calls referenced by the texts graphics.library and intuition.library. Each result is stored in a global, and a fallback routine runs when a result is zero.

name: wait_for_status_then_call
description: Repeatedly calls a routine until it returns one of the values one, two or three, then passes a global pointer and a frame-relative address to another routine.

name: load_pic_and_classify
description: Loads the picture named load.pic through library calls, then waits within a bounded loop of about 350000 iterations for a flag to clear. It then classifies two stored shorts into one of three ranges and returns a code from zero to three.

name: init_callbacks_and_run_loop
description: Stores two routine addresses and three constants in globals, then clears a word table and initializes sixteen slot records. It loops while a flag is set, calling routines on each pass to update the two slot groups.

name: interpret_script_opcodes
description: Reads bytes from a script buffer one at a time. Small values are used as positions or timings, while values in the upper range act as opcodes that record entries in short tables and call other routines with computed values. The listing is cut off partway, so the remaining opcodes cannot be recovered.

name: return_immediately
description: Contains only a return, so calling it performs no work.

name: init_slots_and_animate
description: Sets up eighteen slot values, each masked to a small range, then repeatedly repositions the slots at offsets computed from the stored values. It loops until a flag clears or a counter reaches zero, and returns zero or one depending on which exit path is taken.

name: fill_two_slot_arrays
description: For each of the given entries, stores one value reduced modulo thirteen and offset by 232 in one array, and one value reduced modulo nine in a second array. Both values come from calls to another routine.

name: advance_slot_arrays
description: Walks the given number of entries and updates each paired counter and value. The counter is increased by one, and when the value would go negative the counter is halved and the value is cleared. The first counter that was set is returned.

name: run_demo_pic_loop
description: Makes a series of setup calls, including one with the fixed value 20072, then calls routines repeatedly while a call returns nonzero and the stop flags stay clear. It copies two globals afterwards and clears a flag pointer before returning. The text demo.pic is referenced.

name: setup_four_plane_pointers
description: Computes four pairs of addresses from a base, stepping the first by three hundred and the second by thirty-two thousand each time, and passes each pair to another routine. It then copies four globals into fixed slots.

name: read_fixed_block_into_buffer
description: Obtains a handle through a call with a fixed code and returns minus one when it is zero. Otherwise it reads thirty-two thousand bytes into the buffer held in a global, passes the buffer on, and releases the handle.

name: load_asset_data_files
description: Opens handles and reads fixed-size blocks into buffers held in globals, referencing the texts font.dat, land0 and sprites0.dat. Each handle is released after its read.

name: read_data_block_with_header
description: Obtains a handle through a call with a fixed code, and when it is valid reads forty thousand bytes into the caller's buffer and sixty-four bytes into a second buffer. It then releases the handle.

name: draw_shifted_words_to_planes
description: Returns early when the vertical position is outside the playfield. Otherwise, for each row of a fixed count, it rotates four bitplane words from a table by the low nibble of the horizontal position and merges them into the destination with an AND mask followed by an OR.

name: draw_shifted_tile_block
description: Checks the row against the playfield bounds, then for sixteen rows reads source words from a fixed table address indexed by the parameter. It rotates each word by the low nibble of the horizontal position and merges four bitplane words into the destination.

name: forward_call_keep_registers
description: Calls another routine and returns whatever the two data registers hold, passing the register-pair result through unchanged.

name: draw_masked_block_to_planes
description: Checks the row against the playfield bounds, then for up to twenty-four rows combines words from a block in globals into four bitplanes. When the horizontal shift is zero it merges the words unshifted; otherwise it rotates them first.

name: rotate_entry_fields_in_table
description: Walks 1680 records of twenty bytes in a global table and rearranges their words and bytes by shifting and copying fields between positions. The changed values are written back in place.

name: shift_byte_buffer_left_three
description: Shifts each of one hundred bytes in a fixed buffer left by three bits, in place.

name: iterate_ten_by_ten_grid
description: Loops over a ten-by-ten grid of cells and calls another routine for each cell, with coordinates derived from the cell's row and column, a global byte offset and a value from a table. When a second global flag byte is set, it calls a further routine for that cell.

name: forward_call_return_registers
description: Calls another routine and returns the values left in the two data registers as one 64-bit result.

name: store_global_address_pointer
description: Stores the address of a global data area into another global pointer variable and has no other effect.

name: render_string_into_bitplanes
description: Clears a table and a block of words, measures the zero-terminated text held in a global pointer, and draws each character as eight rows of glyph bytes from a font table into five planes spaced by three hundred twenty bytes. The global pointer is advanced past the text. The text POPULOUS is referenced.

name: install_interrupt_handler_and_enable
description: Obtains a base through a library call and, when it is valid, writes a mask that disables all interrupts, stores a handler routine and then writes a mask that re-enables selected interrupts. When the base is not available it calls the cleanup routines and returns.

name: install_interrupt_handler_and_enable
description: Obtains a base through a library call and, when it is valid, writes a mask that disables all interrupts, stores a handler routine and then writes a mask that re-enables selected interrupts. When the base is not available it calls the cleanup routines and returns.

name: transfer_to_interrupt_setup
description: Single-instruction entry that transfers control to another routine. The listing supplied is the larger body that routine runs, which disables interrupts, installs a handler and re-enables selected interrupts.

name: install_interrupt_handler_and_enable
description: Obtains a base through a library call and, when it is valid, writes a mask that disables all interrupts, stores a handler routine and then writes a mask that re-enables selected interrupts. When the base is not available it calls the cleanup routines and returns.

name: install_interrupt_handler_and_enable
description: Obtains a base through a library call and, when it is valid, writes a mask that disables all interrupts, stores a handler routine and then writes a mask that re-enables selected interrupts. When the base is not available it calls the cleanup routines and returns.

name: load_popsam_sample_file
description: Opens the dos library and the file named popsam, allocates memory for it and reads it in. It shows an alert text for a missing file or a failed allocation, and it writes the interrupt-enable registers around the transfer.

name: return_immediately
description: Contains only a return, so calling it performs no work.

name: clear_flag_byte_and_return
description: Clears one byte at a fixed offset from the pointer argument and returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack unchanged.

name: restore_saved_interrupt_masks
description: Writes a mask that disables all interrupts, calls a routine through a function pointer, then restores three saved register values. It writes the saved enable value with the enable flag bit set and returns the register-pair result unchanged.

name: dispatch_and_clear_flag
description: Compares a one-byte argument with the values ten and one and calls a routine for each match. It then clears a flag byte at a fixed offset from the object pointer and returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack.

name: clear_flag_after_conditional_call
description: Calls a routine only when the one-byte argument equals one, then clears a flag byte at a fixed offset from the object pointer and returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack.

name: clear_flag_byte_and_return
description: Clears one byte at a fixed offset from the object pointer and returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack unchanged.

name: clear_flag_byte_and_return
description: Clears one byte at a fixed offset from the object pointer and returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack unchanged.

name: clear_flag_byte_and_return
description: Clears one byte at a fixed offset from the object pointer and returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack unchanged.

name: clear_flag_byte_and_return
description: Clears one byte at a fixed offset from the object pointer and returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack unchanged.

name: acknowledge_status_bit_interrupt
description: Tests one status bit in a global word and, when it is set, writes all ones to a fixed byte address, stores masked values back into globals and calls another routine. The facts list the CIA and interrupt request registers as touched, so this is an interrupt acknowledgement.

name: build_period_tables_from_records
description: Reads eight six-byte records from a table, storing for each a link value, a halved size and a period computed by dividing a fixed clock constant by the record's word. It then converts two stored link values into addresses and fills four entries of a second table.

name: build_period_tables_from_records
description: Reads eight six-byte records from a table, storing for each a link value, a halved size and a period computed by dividing a fixed clock constant by the record's word. It then converts two stored link values into addresses and fills four entries of a second table.

name: clear_audio_control_state
description: Clears one global byte and writes two constant values to a global control word. The facts link the word to the audio control and DMA control registers, and the routine returns without further work.

name: update_sound_channels
description: When its enable byte is set, steps through four sound channels from the last to the first. For each channel it writes the audio location, length, period and volume registers, and sets the matching DMA bit when a sample starts. Sequence bytes select samples, change the envelope, jump to a loop position or set modulation flags.

name: step_sound_channel_sequence
description: Advances one channel's sequence by decoding script bytes that start a sample, set a flag, jump to a loop position or change the envelope. It writes the channel's audio registers and continues down through the channels until the index underflows.

name: restart_sound_channel_sequence
description: Resets a channel's state bytes and reads its sequence from the start. It processes the same opcode set, writes the audio registers for each step, and moves on to the next channel when the sequence finishes.

name: start_sound_channel_sequence
description: Takes a table index from the sequence, points the channel's envelope at the matching entry, and then decodes the sequence. It writes the audio registers and continues down through the channels until the index underflows.

name: play_sound_channel_sequence
description: Begins a channel's sequence from a stored offset and feeds the same opcode decoder, writing the hardware channel registers and updating the sequence position. Processing continues until the channel index underflows.

name: enter_sound_sequencer_loop
description: Single-instruction entry that jumps into the shared sound sequencer loop, which decodes per-channel script bytes and writes the audio channel registers.

name: enter_sound_sequencer_loop
description: Stores a control byte in a channel record, marks the channel, and then joins the shared sound sequencer loop, which decodes script bytes and writes the audio channel registers.

name: read_sequence_pointer_and_decode
description: Loads the next sequence position for a channel from a stored pointer table and continues into the shared sound sequencer decoder, which writes the audio registers.

name: start_sample_on_channel
description: Writes the sample address, length, period and volume for a channel to its audio registers, sets the matching DMA bit, and then runs the sequencer loop. The facts list the DMA control register as touched.

name: apply_envelope_to_channel
description: Each tick, adds a stored slope to the channel volume when a flag is set, scales a period value by a table entry, and writes the volume register. It also advances a position counter that writes a byte into a stored buffer.

name: clear_channel_buffer_and_sequence
description: Entry that clears one byte of a channel's stored buffer at the current position and records the position, then joins the shared sound sequencer loop that writes the audio channel registers.

name: clear_buffer_to_limit
description: Steps the buffer position down by one and, while it is still above a stored limit, clears a flag bit and writes a zero byte into the buffer at that position. It then joins the shared sound sequencer loop.

name: write_buffer_byte_and_sequence
description: Writes the value sixty into the channel buffer at the current position, records the position, and joins the shared sound sequencer loop that writes the audio registers.

name: blend_bitplanes_with_mask_cycle
description: Iterates over sixty-four rows of four bitplane words, choosing a mask word from a cycle of three globals on each step. Each word is blended with the source using that mask, and the result is stored in place.

name: blend_source_row_into_planes
description: Walks 160 source words in order, combining each with a mask taken from a three-entry cycle in globals. Each result is written into four bitplanes, using an AND with the complement followed by an OR for each plane.

name: store_stack_word_and_call
description: Copies a word passed on the stack into a global variable and then calls another routine.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls another routine and returns. The decompiled listing contains only that call followed by the return.

name: update_mouse_pointer_position
description: Checks a status bit, then computes horizontal and vertical movement from the difference between the current mouse counter bytes and the saved ones. Each difference is wrapped to a signed byte and added to the pointer position, which is clamped on the horizontal axis to a range of zero to six hundred thirty-nine and then halved. The facts list the joystick data register and CIA registers as touched.

name: save_mouse_counter_bytes
description: Splits the mouse counter word into its low and high bytes and saves them in globals for the next movement update. The facts list the joystick data register as read.

name: save_handler_and_enable_interrupts
description: Copies a global word into a stored routine slot and a memory cell, then writes an enable mask with the enable flag bit set. The facts list the interrupt enable registers as touched.

name: restore_pending_interrupt_mask
description: When a stored value is nonzero, writes a mask that disables all interrupts, writes the stored value back, then writes it again with the enable flag bit set. It clears the stored value and returns the global word read afterwards, or zero when nothing was stored. The facts list the interrupt enable and request registers.

name: build_copper_list
description: Fills a memory block with a copper list. It writes fixed display control and bitplane register words, selects one of two display window pairs by a global flag, then writes thirty-two register-value pairs from a table, starting at the first colour register and stepping by two.

name: set_copper_location_and_wait
description: Stores its parameter in a global slot, writes a value four greater to the copper location register, then polls the interrupt request read-back until the vertical blank bit is set. It returns the masked result.

name: wait_for_vertical_blank
description: Clears the vertical blank request by writing its bit to the interrupt request register, then polls the read-back until the bit is set again. It returns the masked bit.

name: fill_copper_color_entries
description: Scans a register-value list until it reaches the marker word for the first colour register, then writes a counted run of values from a second array into the following register slots, stepping by two words each time.

name: process_undecoded_routine_body
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this twenty-one instruction routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered from the evidence. The recorded facts show only that one unnamed routine calls it.

name: set_entry_position_control_bytes
description: Computes start and stop values from its two position arguments, adjusting the vertical start by an offset that depends on a global flag. It then writes the position bytes and the high-bit flags into the control block of an entry chosen from a table.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_byte
description: Reads keyboard codes from the keyboard controller's serial data register and tracks a flag for the key state. When the flag is clear and a key is detected, it inverts the raw code, turns it into a table index and looks up the character, which is held in a table of text including the digits row. It clears the flag when the key is released.

name: copy_eight_thousand_longwords
description: Copies eight thousand 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block, one at a time.

name: decrement_nibble_fields_until_zero
description: Copies thirty-two words of input into a stack buffer and repeatedly decrements each nonzero four-bit field in each word, looping while any field changed. The facts list the vertical raster position register as read and two routines as callees.

name: call_then_forward_with_args
description: Calls one routine with no arguments, then calls a second routine with its two parameters and returns the second routine's result.

name: forward_then_conditional_call
description: Passes its parameter to one routine, then calls a second routine only when a stored word in the global frame is nonzero.

name: advance_seed_word
description: Adds the constant twelve thousand three hundred forty-five to a value returned by a routine, stores the sum in a global longword, and returns its high word with the top bit cleared.

name: store_high_word_argument
description: Stores the upper sixteen bits of its argument into a global longword. The routine is marked unreached, and the library calls listed in its facts do not appear in the listing.

name: return_immediately
description: Contains only a return, so calling it performs no work.

name: allocate_tagged_record_block
description: Allocates a record sized from a global index, and returns early when the allocation fails. Otherwise it sets the record's fields, writes a four-character tag into it, and calls a wrapper that gets the current directory to complete the record.

name: allocate_and_build_name_string
description: Chooses a base string, either a global default or one taken from the object's table entry, and allocates a buffer sized to the base length plus the parameter. When the allocation succeeds it copies the base text into the buffer and calls other routines to finish the name. Four routines are called.

name: append_string_bounded
description: Appends the second zero-terminated string to the end of the first, copying at most about thirty-two thousand characters and terminating the result. It returns the first pointer.

name: append_string_with_count
description: Appends the second zero-terminated string to the first, copying at most the count given in the third argument and then terminating the result. It returns the first pointer.

name: copy_string_and_zero_pad
description: Copies a zero-terminated string up to the given count, then fills the rest of the destination with zero bytes. It returns the destination pointer.

name: compute_high_half_product
description: Computes the cross-product sum of the 16-bit halves of its two arguments, shifted into the high word, and returns it as the upper half of a 64-bit result. The second argument is returned as the lower half.

name: open_icon_library_window_entry
description: Opens the icon library, then uses it to obtain a window-related entry and a file handle, storing both in the object. The texts WINDOW and icon.library are referenced. The library is released before returning.

name: call_hook_then_forward
description: Calls a function pointer held in a global when it is set, then calls another routine with no arguments.

name: call_hook_then_forward
description: Calls a function pointer held in a global when it is set, then calls another routine with no arguments.

name: release_table_and_locks
description: Frees a table of entries when present by calling a release routine for each one, then releases a second held resource. It stores a saved value through a pointer, closes the remaining handles and calls the supervisor and unlock wrappers.

name: close_indexed_file_slot
description: Checks a slot index against the table size and whether the slot holds a handle. For an invalid index or an empty slot it sets an error code and returns minus one. Otherwise it closes the handle unless a flag in the slot is set, clears the slot, and returns zero.

name: call_close_wrapper
description: Jumps through a library vector at a fixed offset of minus thirty-six from a library base held in a global. The facts identify the target as the close wrapper, and the routine returns after the call.

name: call_open_wrapper
description: Calls the library open function through a vector at a fixed offset of minus thirty from a library base held in a global, passing the caller's arguments on.

name: call_library_vector_414
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus four hundred fourteen from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_414
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus four hundred fourteen from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_198
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus one hundred ninety-eight from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_198
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus one hundred ninety-eight from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_294
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus two hundred ninety-four from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_294
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus two hundred ninety-four from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_132
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus one hundred thirty-two from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_132
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus one hundred thirty-two from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_210
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus two hundred ten from a library base held in a global. The facts show it reaches the library stub at that offset.

name: call_library_vector_372
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus three hundred seventy-two from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_552
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus five hundred fifty-two from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_552
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus five hundred fifty-two from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_138
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus one hundred thirty-eight from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_366
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus three hundred sixty-six from a library base held in a global. The entry is marked unreached.

name: call_library_vector_384
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus three hundred eighty-four from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_96
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus ninety-six from a library base held in a different global. It returns after the call.

name: call_library_vector_78
description: Calls the library function at a vector offset of minus seventy-eight from a library base held in a global. It returns after the call.

name: halt_on_unimplemented_entry
description: Entry that only halts on an unimplemented instruction, so the decoded listing is a halt marker rather than behaviour.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls another routine and returns. The decompiled listing contains only that call followed by the return.

name: call_pointer_from_structure
description: Loads the first longword of the structure passed in the address register and calls the routine it points to.

name: update_countdown_entry
description: Writes a stored value into a field reached through the entry's link pointer, installs the handler, and decrements a countdown word in the entry. When the countdown reaches zero it clears the word or resets the entry's links, depending on the value read before the decrement.

name: unlink_entry_and_update_counts
description: Writes a stored value through the entry's link pointer when a flag is set, then unlinks the entry from a doubly linked list and decrements a countdown word. When the countdown reaches zero it either clears the state or moves the entry to the next stored record.

name: advance_countdown_list_entry
description: Decrements a countdown word in the entry. When it reaches zero it either clears the entry's state or moves the entry onto the next record in its linked list, copying the record's values and storing the handler.

name: store_entry_status_and_notify
description: Stores the entry's link value and a status word with the top bit set into an owner structure. It returns early when the link points back to itself and a flag is clear; otherwise it clears the flag where needed and calls a global routine.

name: unlink_and_store_entry_status
description: Copies two status words into the owner structure and unlinks the entry from its list when a link is set. It returns early when no work is pending, and otherwise calls a global routine.

name: reset_entry_and_notify
description: Clears a field of the entry, stores the handler, and copies a status word to the owner. It then returns early or calls a global routine, following the same tail as the other list handlers.

name: select_list_record_or_reset
description: Resets the entry's count and copies a status word to the owner when the carry flag is set. Otherwise it takes the first record from the entry's linked list and copies its values into the entry. It calls two routines.

name: take_first_list_record
description: Takes the first record from the entry's linked list, copies its size and data words into the entry, relinks the list, and stores the handler. It then sets a status word on the owner and calls routines.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls another routine and returns. The decompiled listing contains only that call followed by the return. The facts list the custom chip base as touched.

name: forward_call_and_return

name: clear_flag_and_cause_interrupt
description: Clears bit one of a flag byte in the entry, calls another routine, then calls a routine through a global base. The facts show the wrapper for the exec Cause function among the callees.

name: remove_list_node_and_reset
description: Removes the node from the list it belongs to by relinking its neighbours, then resets the node's own links to point at itself and clears its second field.

name: drain_list_with_interrupt_guard
description: While the list head is non-null, removes the first node and raises a nesting counter in the base structure. Each pass writes an interrupt-disable mask, calls a library routine at a vector offset of minus three hundred seventy-eight, and lowers the counter, re-enabling interrupts when it reaches zero.

name: decrement_counter_and_enable_interrupts
description: Reads a byte at an offset in the base structure, decrements it and writes it back. If the byte was zero or one before the decrement, it writes an interrupt mask with the enable bit set, which enables interrupts.

name: initialize_audio_device_block
description: Sets a control value, stores its argument and initializes three sub-lists. It writes default channel values, then calls the exec SetIntVector wrapper to install an interrupt vector. The text audio.device is referenced and the DMA control register is touched.

name: set_field_and_forward
description: Writes the byte value 254 into a field of the first argument's structure and calls another routine with the second argument's offset structure and the first argument.

name: add_request_to_list_tail
description: Writes the byte value 254 into a field of the first argument, then adds that structure to the tail of a list through the add-tail wrapper.

name: link_request_and_update_registers
description: When the request has a non-null link and its flag bit is clear, moves the link into the second word, installs the handler, and writes a status word to the control register. Otherwise it calls a routine for the other case.

name: store_request_status_and_enable
description: Moves the request's link into its second word and installs the handler. It writes the request's status to the control register, setting the enable bit when the status bit was clear, and writes a second status word to the interrupt control register.

name: process_linked_request_chain
description: Follows a link field of the structure, calling a routine on the current structure and then on the linked structure when that link differs from another field. It returns no value.

name: move_listed_request_to_tail
description: Walks the list for the given node. When it is found, it removes the node and re-adds it to the tail of the list in the base, unless its flag byte is one. It then sets the flag to 254 and returns one; otherwise it returns zero.

name: scan_list_then_move_request
description: Walks a list from a given node looking for a target node. When the target is found, it moves the target to the tail of the list in the base unless its flag byte is one, sets the flag to 254 and returns one. When the walk ends it returns zero.

name: locate_request_then_move
description: Walks a list from its head looking for the target node. When it is found, it moves the node to the tail of the list in the base unless its flag byte is one, sets its flag to 254 and returns one. It returns zero when the target is absent.

name: mark_list_requests_and_dispatch
description: Walks a list and writes the byte value 254 into a flag field of every node. It calls a routine on the first node when the list is nonempty, with the wrapper for disable called before and after the walk.

name: mark_chain_flags_and_dispatch
description: Walks a chain of nodes from a given node, writing the byte value 254 into the flag field of each. It calls the disable wrapper before and after the walk, and calls a routine when the list head is present.

name: stop_request_and_clear_bit
description: Calls the disable wrapper, then calls routines on the argument and on fields at two offsets of it. It clears bit one of a status word in the argument and returns.

name: write_table_value_to_adkcon
description: Calls two routines to set up the argument, stores a fixed longword in an indexed slot, and writes a value from a byte table into the audio control register. It then clears bit zero of a status word in the argument. The facts list the audio control register as touched.

name: store_table_byte_and_call
description: Stores a byte from a table indexed by a register into the memory location one byte before the argument, then calls a library function through a vector offset of minus thirty from a library base held in the structure.

name: initialize_list_head
description: Initializes an empty list head: points its first word at itself, clears the second word and points the third word at itself.

name: forbid_multitasking
description: Calls the exec Forbid function through the library vector at offset minus one hundred thirty-two from the exec base held in a global, which suspends task switching.

name: free_memory_block_via_exec
description: Calls the exec FreeMem function through the library vector at offset minus two hundred ten from the exec base held in a global.

name: increment_count_clear_bit
description: Increments a word counter at a fixed offset of the object and clears bit three of a status byte at another offset.

name: decrement_count_and_check_flag
description: Decrements a word counter at a fixed offset of the object. When it reaches zero and bit three of a status byte is set, it calls a routine and returns that result. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: unlink_and_free_request
description: When the counter at a fixed offset is zero, unlinks the object from its list, reads its stored value and frees its memory through the library vector at offset minus two hundred ten. Otherwise it sets bit three of a status byte and returns zero.

name: set_flag_bit_and_return
description: Sets bit three of a status byte in the object and returns zero.

name: record_request_pointer_or_alert
description: Stores its arguments in fields of the object, then calls a library function at offset minus four hundred eight. When the result is zero it calls the alert routine; otherwise it saves two values into globals.

name: copy_two_fields_to_globals
description: Copies two longword fields from the object into two global variables.

name: store_argument_in_result_field
description: Library code that calls a function through a vector offset of minus two hundred ninety-four from a base taken from the first argument's structure, then stores the second argument at offset one hundred forty-eight of the returned object.

name: chain_two_calls_with_cleanup
description: Library code that calls one routine and, when it returns a nonzero value, calls a second routine with that value. If the second call fails it calls a cleanup routine on the first result and returns zero; otherwise it returns the first result.

name: read_icon_record_fields
description: Library code that obtains a record through one call and fills a local buffer through a second call. It copies ten longwords and eight further fields from that buffer into the record and links the record back into the structure when a field is set. When the second call fails it releases the record and returns zero.

name: copy_frame_fields_into_object
description: Library code that copies a block of ten longwords from the stack frame into the object, then copies several further single fields into fixed offsets of the object, and calls one other routine.

name: return_zero_value
description: Returns zero and performs no other work.

name: build_icon_header_and_copy
description: Library code that writes a fixed magic word and a version word into a local buffer, copies ten longwords and several fields from the object into it, then calls one other routine.

name: load_info_file_into_icon
description: Library code that builds a name in a 260-byte buffer from its arguments and the text .info, opens it through the library vector at offset minus thirty, and loads its contents with several further calls.

name: validate_icon_header_and_load
description: Library code that checks a header word against the icon magic value and a version word of one, then clears two result words. When a linked field is set it loads the linked records through further calls, and returns a result from those checks.
